title: Corporate Memphis
summary: Flat cartoon people with small heads, long bendy limbs, and purple or blue skin. The friendly face of Big Tech.
lede: A flat vector illustration style that tech companies used from about 2017 to the early 2020s: smiling figures with small heads, long elastic arms and legs, and skin in non-natural colors such as purple, blue, or pink, drawn in solid fills with no outlines or texture. The design agency Buck made the core example, the *Alegria* illustration system for Facebook (2017). Mike Merrill named the style after the Memphis Group in the title of an Are.na board, but it has almost nothing in common with that group’s work.

era.note: Facebook introduced Buck’s Alegria system in 2017. AIGA Eye on Design (2019) and Wired (2021) describe the style as everywhere in tech. Wikipedia cites Creative Bloq that by 2023 its popularity had fallen and it was used as parody. Free libraries such as Humaaans and unDraw keep it in use.

attestation.label: AIGA Eye on Design, Rachel Hawley, “Don’t Worry, These Gangly-armed Cartoons Are Here to Protect You From Big Tech” (21 August 2019)
Wired, Josh Gabert-Doyon, “Why does every advert look the same? Blame Corporate Memphis” (24 January 2021)
Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute: Corporate Memphis

lineage.note: Named after the Memphis Group (Wikidata P138 on Q105676972). The Consumer Aesthetics Research Institute states that the style “rarely carries any resemblance” to the group’s work. The shared traits are bright color and geometric shapes, not pattern or furniture form.

Wikipedia dates the roots of the style to 2013, when Apple moved from skeuomorphism to flat design. The figures use the same solid fills, with no gradient, gloss, or texture, and the illustrations sit in flat interfaces.
Wikipedia lists Material Design as a Google design language linked to Corporate Memphis. Google products and marketing used both at the same time.

Wikipedia names Frutiger Aero as the prominent style that came before Corporate Memphis. Frutiger Aero is glossy, photographic, and skeuomorphic. Corporate Memphis replaced it with flat cartoon figures.

lineage.label: Modernist figure distortion
lineage.note: Wikipedia compares the exaggerated proportions with modernist paintings such as Matisse’s *The Dance* (1910), and CARI lists Matisse-influenced graphics among the traits. This is a comparison, not a documented line of descent.

grammar.text: Cartoon people with small heads, long elastic arms and legs, large hands and feet, and simple torsos. AIGA Eye on Design describes limbs “arching away from their bodies like giant wet noodles”. Faces have few features or none.

Skin is purple, blue, pink, orange, or green. The Buck illustrator Xoana Herrera describes the characters as “ethnically non-specific”. The rest of the palette is a small set of bright solid colors on white or a pale pastel.
Solid fills with no outlines, no texture, and no shading, or one flat shadow tone at most. Wired quotes the illustrator Jack Hurley on its “simple shapes [and] untextured colours”.
Bodies are built from circles, pills, and rounded blocks, so many artists and libraries can make matching figures. Humaaans (Pablo Stanley, 2018) sells this as mix-and-match heads, tops, and legs.
Figures dance, run, high-five, water plants, or carry oversized objects such as a pencil, a trombone, or a calendar. In animation the long limbs swing and bend.

Scenes fill hero areas, onboarding screens, and empty, error, and success states on a white or pale page. Pastel blobs and potted plants sit behind the figures. The interface around them uses rounded cards and pill buttons.

Headings are a bold geometric or rounded sans-serif in sentence case. CARI lists geometric sans typefaces among the traits of the friendly corporate look. The type supports the illustration and does not carry the style.

synthesis: The template is Buck’s [Alegria](ref:facebook-alegria-illustration-system-2017) system for Facebook (2017). Its style guide fixes the rules that made the look easy to copy: circle heads, cylinder limbs, figures 11½ heads tall, and non-natural skin. Free kits then spread it: [Humaaans](ref:humaaans-illustration-library-2018) (2018) sells mix-and-match parts under CC0, and Wired names [unDraw](ref:undraw-illustration-library) with Freepik and Adobe’s library. [Katharina Brenner’s illustration](ref:brenner-big-tech-cartoons-illustration-2019) for AIGA, built from Humaaans parts, is the image most sources use for the style, and a [Wikimedia research deck](ref:wikimedia-android-microcontributions-report-2019) shows the same parts used as ready-made decoration.

Not every Big Tech illustration system of the period joined in. Airbnb’s head of illustration [rejected the rainbow-colored figures](ref:airbnb-illustration-guidelines-2018) as “not real”, and [Slack’s 2018 site](ref:slack-website-2018) and [Fastmail’s 2020 site](ref:fastmail-website-2020) keep the flat, long-limbed figures with natural skin and some texture. Later uses add outlines and patterns: the [WikiCon Brasil 2022](ref:wikicon-brasil-2022-figure) identity, a [Firefox Pocket illustration](ref:firefox-pocket-rainbow-reader-2020), and a [Catalan government video](ref:generalitat-catalunya-election-video-2024). The game [Going Under](ref:going-under-video-game-2020) (2020) turns the palette and props into satire.

The clearest websites are Wayback copies from 2018: [Twist](ref:twist-website-2018), [Stasher](ref:stasher-website-2018), and [Airtable](ref:airtable-website-2018). [TokyWoky 2020](ref:tokywoky-website-2020), [JotForm 2018](ref:jotform-website-2018), and the live [Jotform](ref:jotform-website) are borderline. Of about twenty live SaaS sites captured in September 2026, only Jotform came close, which supports the sources that date the style’s decline to about 2023.

The style lives in the illustration, not in the CSS. The three clear sites have a median corner radius of 0, medium-weight headings, and small shadows on 12–38% of boxes, so the first fingerprint (set from the specimen: pill shapes, radius 20 px or more, no shadows) failed all of them. The calibrated fingerprint measures the screenshot instead: several bright hues, a saturated strongest color, a high average chroma, and a white or pale page. Twist fails it because its figures use one blue family, and Fastmail and JotForm 2018 fail because their heroes are full-bleed color fields.

diagnostic: People are drawn with small heads and long, bendy arms and legs.
Skin is a non-natural color such as purple, blue, pink, or green.
Shapes are solid fills with no outlines, texture, or shading.
Figures act out an activity, often with an oversized object: a pencil, a phone, a leaf, or a speech bubble.
The illustration sits on a white or pale page, often in front of a pastel blob.
counter: Ink outlines, hatching, or grain texture on the figures.
Realistic proportions and natural skin tones throughout.
Photography, 3D rendering, or gloss carries the images.
Laminate patterns, squiggles, and toy-like furniture without figures. This points to Memphis.
An interface of color fields and glyph icons with no illustrated people. This points to flat design.

confusions.difference: Memphis is about laminate pattern, clashing color, and toy-like object form, and has no gangly figures. Corporate Memphis borrows the name, not the look.
Flat design is an interface style of solid color tiles and glyph icons. Corporate Memphis is an illustration style of people. A flat interface without figures is flat design.
Material Design lifts cards and buttons with shadows. Its product illustrations sometimes use flat figures, but the style of the interface is not the style of the illustration.
Mid-century figures are geometric, often outlined, and printed in warm, muted colors on paper. Corporate Memphis figures have smooth vector fills, bright saturated colors, and long bendy limbs.
A variant draws the same flat figures in isometric projection with buildings and devices. Treat it as Corporate Memphis when the figures have the gangly proportions.

do: Draw people from simple shapes: a small circle for the head, a rounded block for the torso, and long, curved limbs.
Give skin a non-natural color such as violet, blue, pink, or green, and keep hair and trousers in the dark text color.
Show each figure doing something with an oversized object, such as a pencil, a phone, or a leaf.
Put the illustration on a white or warm white page, in front of a pastel blob.
Use a small palette: one strong violet or blue, a coral, a yellow, and a green for plants.
Round every card, panel, and button. Use pill shapes for buttons and inputs.
Use a bold geometric sans-serif for headings in sentence case.
dont: Do not outline shapes. Separate them by color.
Do not add texture, grain, gradients, or glossy highlights.
Do not use drop shadows on cards or buttons.
Do not draw detailed faces or realistic proportions.
Do not fill backgrounds with repeating patterns. That points to Memphis.
Do not let figures overlap body text. Keep the illustration in its own area.
avoid: Brands that need a distinct voice. Many readers now see the style as generic Big Tech.
Audiences that distrust large technology companies.
Luxury, editorial, and serious cultural brands.

fingerprint.note: The illustrations use several bright hues at once, such as violet skin, a yellow shirt, coral shoes, and green leaves. Measured on screenshot pixels so that colors in SVG and image illustrations count. Checked 2026-09-28: the clear captures of Stasher (5) and Airtable (6) pass; Twist (2) fails because its figures are drawn in one blue family.

The strongest color on the page is a saturated illustration color, not a muted accent. Calibrated 2026-09-28 on the clear captures Twist 2018 (0.64), Stasher 2018 (0.68), and Airtable 2018 (0.65); the specimen measures 0.67.

The colored illustration fills a large part of the first screen, so the average screenshot chroma is well above a white page with small accents. Added 2026-09-28 from the clear captures Twist 2018 (0.07), Stasher 2018 (0.12), and Airtable 2018 (0.09); the specimen measures 0.09. It separates the style from white pages with a few bright icons (0.03–0.04).

The illustration sits on a white or very pale page. Calibrated 2026-09-28 on the clear captures Twist 2018 (0.94), Stasher 2018 (0.92), and Airtable 2018 (0.93); the specimen measures 0.92. Pages with a full-bleed color hero, such as Fastmail 2020 (0.82), fail.
Headings are a medium to heavy sans-serif, never light. Lowered from 600 on 2026-09-28: all three clear captures (Twist, Stasher, Airtable, 2018) set headings at 500.

Flat illustration does not mean a shadowless interface. Widened from 0.05 on 2026-09-28: the clear captures measure 0.23 (Twist), 0.38 (Stasher), and 0.12 (Airtable), from small shadows on search bars, fields, and cards. Heavy shadow on most boxes still points to Material Design or neumorphism.
Solid fills only, no gradients. Checked 2026-09-28: Stasher and Airtable measure 0; Twist 2018 (0.46) fails on CSS gradients outside the illustration.
